newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- NY/NJ Port bonds repriced.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- NY/NJ Port bonds repriced.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were flat to down 1/8 of a point at midday as Lehman Brothers priced and repriced a $943 million Port Authority of New York and New Jersey deal.
The top yield in 2025 was lowered to 6.10 percent from 6.14 percent.

"It seems like they had it all institutionally done before they ever showed the Street," one trader said. "It didn't allow for anybody else to make money but the managers. So it's a little tough, but everybody's in that position any more. If they've got it, the want to keep it for themselves."
Various traders said they thought preliminary pricing was on target.
"The deal should be in great shape," one trader said, adding that it was "very fairly priced."
After the repricing, however, another trader thought the deal was too expensive. She conceded that demand probably existed at the higher levels.
"To bump it like that they probably had a consensus (that) there was interest institutionally," the trader said.

Back in secondary market action, traders described the market as flat to perhaps down 1/8 point on the long end, though one trader saw more weakness with prices down 3/8 of a point in spots. All agreed that action was extremely quiet as the Port Authority deal dominated market focus.

Friday's actively quoted issues included Delaware River Port Authority of Pennslyvania and New Jersey 5-1/2 percent bonds of January 2026. The bonds had a 5.87 percent net bid, unchanged from Thursday.

In debt futures the June Municipal contract was down 3/32 at 112-6/32. The June T-bond contract was down 4/32 at 107-6/32. In the U.S. government cash market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 3/32 at 93-22/32 to yield 7.14 percent. The MOB spread was 160 ticks.
